_readme: Ep.01, vertical. This is NOT a second edit — it extends edit-plan.json, so the
cut, the phrase anchors, the B-roll picks and the argument are the same file.
Only what is genuinely frame-dependent lives here.
Full-bleed: the footage is cropped to the speaker and fills the frame, cards
overlay it — what a vertical feed expects. The cost is real and worth stating:
the A-roll was shot 1280x720, so a 9:16 crop is 405x720 of actual pixels
scaled 2.67x. The builder does that crop and scale itself with lanczos plus a
light unsharp instead of leaving the renderer to stretch a video element
bilinearly, which is the difference between acceptable and mushy. The 4K
B-roll is unaffected.
arollFit: "band" is the alternative — the footage at 1:1 in a window with the
cards in the room underneath, which is sharper but gives up the full-frame
look. Built and documented in PIPELINE.md; not what this episode ships.
The builder handles the rest on its own: side-by-side layouts stack
(compare:versus -> stack, timeline:track -> rows, endcard:split -> center),
panels go full-width and sit low in the frame, display type scales to the
narrower frame, captions run bigger, and the face guard is re-measured through
the crop so nothing lands on his eyes.
beatOverrides drops b03b, the ring round the scroll wheel. In 16:9 that shot
shows the whole top edge and the ring picks the wheel out of it; the 9:16 crop
is so tight that the wheel already fills the frame, and a ring round the only
thing on screen reads as a mistake. b18's cells row still carries the no-text
beat, so the vertical cut keeps a graphic that works without words.
beatOverrides also set fit:"whole" on the product macros (b02, b12, b19): a
9:16 crop of a 16:9 macro keeps 31.6% of the width and loses the object, so
those fit the frame's WIDTH with a blurred copy of the same frame above and
below. The textures and wides (trays, the line, loose buttons) crop fine.
b14 is the one card that becomes a different TYPE in vertical. In 16:9 the
wheel/ball/pad story is a timeline:track — three stops on a rail, which reads
left to right across a wide frame. On a phone that same card is a list of
short lines. So vertical runs it as plate:slides instead: the three actual
photographs, each arriving on the phrase that calls for it. Same argument,
the form the frame can carry.
b13 drops to a single photograph in vertical. In 16:9 it is a duo (the phone
and a trackball macro); here the trackball and the trackpad both appear in
The BlackBerry story runs across b13 and b14 in vertical: b13 is the wheel-era
phone with the copy, b14 is a two-slide sequence picking up at the ball and
ending on the flat pad. Putting all three in the slideshow repeated b13's
photograph, which lint catches as a duplicate media node and which reads as a
stutter anyway.

b14.intent: vertical: the controls as pictures, one per phrase. b13 has already established the wheel-era phone, so this picks up at the ball — the three-step story told across two cards rather than repeating the same photograph.

card.caption: Then the ball. Then a flat pad.

b13.intent: vertical: one photograph of the phone. The ball and the pad are the slideshow's job at b14, so a duo here showed the same Bold 9700 twice.
